This is a cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study evaluating the ROMA test combination (HE4 and CA125) with histopathological verification as reference standard in women with ovarian masses (pelvic mass).
This is a projection study of cancer incidence and mortality, not a diagnostic test accuracy study evaluating tests for ovarian cancer diagnosis.
This is a qualitative study describing women's experiences with diagnosis, not a diagnostic test accuracy study.
This is a review article discussing ovarian carcinoma heterogeneity and models, not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.

This study evaluates biomarkers for lead time before diagnosis but does not restrict to women with a pelvic mass suspicious for OC; it uses ovarian cancer cases and controls from a general population.
This is a methodological paper describing a tool for quality assessment of diagnostic accuracy studies, not a diagnostic test accuracy study itself.
This study validates the ROMA test combination (CA125, HE4, menopausal status) with histologic diagnosis as reference standard in women with pelvic mass.
This is a review article about CA125, not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.
This is a theoretical model proposal for ovarian carcinogenesis, not a diagnostic test accuracy study.
This is a review article discussing proteomic technologies and biomarkers, not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.
This study validates the RMI test combination with histopathological findings as reference standard in premenopausal and postmenopausal women with adnexal masses (pelvic mass).
This study evaluates the diagnostic accuracy of ROMA test combination with biopsy or clinical follow-up as reference standard in women with pelvic mass.
This study evaluates the discriminative power of expert sonography, CA-125, RMI, and their combinations (test combinations) with surgical histopathology as reference standard.
This study validates the IOTA three-step strategy (a test combination) with histological diagnosis as reference standard in women with adnexal masses.
This is a methodological study evaluating tests for publication bias in meta-analyses of diagnostic test accuracy, not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.

This study evaluates the diagnostic performance of HE4, CA125, and ROMA (test combinations) with histologic verification for early-stage epithelial ovarian cancer detection in women with pelvic masses.
This study validates the IOTA ADNEX model (a multivariable model) for differential diagnosis of adnexal tumors with histologic confirmation as reference standard.
This is a cohort study evaluating outcomes of a testing strategy implementation (symptom triggered testing) on cancer outcomes, not a diagnostic test accuracy study of a specific test or combination.
This study validates a predictive model using HE4 and CA125 (test combination) with histology or follow-up as reference standard in women with pelvic mass.
This is a guideline document for evaluation and management of adnexal masses, not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.
This is a molecular study investigating genetic mutations in ovarian carcinomas, not a diagnostic test accuracy study.

Despite the truncated abstract, the title indicates a comparison of HE4 with traditional tumor markers, suggesting a diagnostic accuracy study evaluating HE4 as a marker for ovarian cancer. Given the context, it likely involves women with ovarian masses or pelvic mass and reference standard histopathology.
This study evaluates HE4 and ROMA (test combination) for distinguishing benign and malignant pelvic masses with histologic verification as reference standard in women with pelvic mass.

Study examines incidence trends of borderline tumors and ovarian cancer over time; does not evaluate diagnostic tests or test combinations for ovarian cancer diagnosis in symptomatic women with pelvic mass.
Study is a systematic review and meta-analysis of existing literature; not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study evaluating test combinations.
Study does not clearly meet selection criteria for diagnostic test accuracy study evaluating test combinations for ovarian cancer diagnosis.

Prospective multicenter cross-sectional study evaluating IOTA LR2 model, ultrasound Simple Rules, RMI, and subjective assessment for preoperative characterization of adnexal masses; compares ≥2 tests with histological reference standard.
Study is a meta-analysis of existing studies on HE4, CA125, and ROMA; not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.

Prospective cross-sectional study evaluating and comparing CA-125, HE4, RMI, and ROMA in preoperative assessment of adnexal masses; uses histopathological diagnosis as gold standard; compares ≥2 tests.

Multicenter study evaluating HE4, CA125, and ROMA as diagnostic tools for ovarian cancer in patients with pelvic mass; assesses performance of single tests and multivariable model (ROMA) with histopathological reference standard.
Paper describes a hierarchical regression approach for meta-analysis of diagnostic test accuracy; not a diagnostic test accuracy study evaluating tests for ovarian cancer.
Paper evaluates performance of hierarchical models for meta-analysis of diagnostic test accuracy with few/sparse data; not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.

Study identifies germline mutations in genes associated with ovarian carcinoma; does not evaluate diagnostic tests or test combinations for ovarian cancer diagnosis in symptomatic women with pelvic mass.
Review article discusses prevalence, etiology, risk factors, diagnosis, and treatment of ovarian cancer; does not present original diagnostic test accuracy data.

Prospective multicenter blinded clinical trial validating ROMA in women with pelvic mass; estimates sensitivity, specificity, NPV, PPV; uses histopathological diagnosis as reference standard; evaluates multivariable model.

Prospective study evaluating four risk of malignancy indices (RMI 1-4) for detection of malignant ovarian tumors; obtains sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, diagnostic accuracy; uses surgical exploration as reference standard; compares ≥2 tests.

Study investigates predictive value of RMI (1-4), CA-125, and inflammatory markers (NLR, PLR) in discriminating ovarian cancers in geriatric and non-geriatric postmenopausal women with adnexal masses; uses histopathological results as reference standard; compares ≥2 tests.

Study evaluates HE4, CA125, and ROMA in preoperative differentiation of benign and malignant adnexal masses; uses histopathological diagnosis as reference standard; assesses performance of single tests and multivariable model (ROMA).
Case-control study identifies and quantifies symptoms of ovarian cancer in primary care; does not evaluate diagnostic tests or test combinations for ovarian cancer diagnosis.

Prospective validation study of ROMA using HE4 and CA125 in women with pelvic mass; analyzes performance of markers and ROMA; uses histopathological diagnosis as reference standard; evaluates multivariable model.
Systematic review and meta-analysis of studies on diagnostic test performance for presurgical diagnosis of adnexal tumours; not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.

Study compares CA125, HE4, ROMA, and RMI for classification of ovarian masses; calculates sensitivity and specificity via ROC curves; uses histopathological diagnosis as reference standard (implied); evaluates ≥2 tests.
Statement from Society of Gynecologic Oncology on risk assessment for inherited gynecologic cancer predispositions; does not evaluate diagnostic test accuracy.

Cross-sectional descriptive study evaluating validity of serum CA-125, HE4, and ROMA at standard and optimal cut-offs for preoperative prediction of epithelial ovarian carcinoma; uses postoperative histopathology as reference standard; evaluates single tests and multivariable model.

Study evaluates HE4 and ROMA index for primary detection of ovarian cancer in postmenopausal Czech women; uses histologically verified diagnoses; assesses diagnostic performance of single test (HE4) and multivariable model (ROMA).

Study evaluates performance of 2D ultrasound and CA125, and added value of 3DPD ultrasound, in predicting malignant/benign ovarian tumors; uses histopathological results as reference standard; considers multiple tests and combinations (RMI, IOTA rules, expert opinion, LR2, 3D vascular indices).
